I wrote the screening output to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/25854.json`. Every cited file:line was read directly; nothing was built or run.

- **Trust decision:** whether the driver may send the clear-text password in the first handshake reply while the TLS server's identity is still unverified (self-signed cert, checked only later by fingerprint). At the pinned commit the only guard is an "is SSL on?" check in `HandshakeResponse.java:141-144`. The fix moves the decision up into `StandardClient.handleAuthentication` (`StandardClient.java:384-395`).
- **`pattern_fit`:** `injection_only`. I found no other unguarded route into the same sink: the auth-switch path is already guarded at `StandardClient.java:474-502`. Realistic spots for planted siblings include the caching_sha2 clear-password branch (`CachingSha2PasswordPlugin.java:212-229`) and a re-authentication or redirect path.
- **Strongest lever:** a believable reason to dismiss. The existing SSL guard in the encoder, plus the later fingerprint and auth-switch checks, make the first-handshake path look covered, but the password has already been sent before any of them runs. A tempting over-broad fix (rejecting every self-signed cert) would break the existing support for self-signed certs with native, ed25519 and parsec logins.
- **Biggest red flag:** this is close to a single-location fix (one function, plus removing a guard in a second file) that takes about 20 minutes. Also, one of the two fix commits (`149ec6a6`) is a backport for an older branch and doesn't apply to this tree, and the PAM case in the new regression test is likely already handled at the pinned commit.
